title: Cerulean Retail POC - batcher & cache budget kickoff
summary: Kickoff to scope a 6-week POC to validate unit economics for Cerulean's conversational shopping assistant. Focus: per-token cost modeling across hosted vs dedicated, batching and KV/prefix cache knobs, hit-rate sensitivity, latency SLOs, and milestone benchmarks. Agreed to three cost scenarios and a small benchmark load to run next week.
topics: KV / prefix cache hit rate assumptions
action_items: Maya Chen - send 3-scenario cost model spreadsheet (hosted / dedicated / hybrid) by 2025-10-24
Ethan Park - prepare micro-benchmark plan and stress script (50, 200, 1000 concurrent) and share run template by 2025-10-23
Raj Patel - provide 7-day sample traffic histogram and top-100 prompt sizes by 2025-10-22
Mira Gomez - provide two canonical prompt templates and golden responses for quality checks by 2025-10-22
next_steps: Run a 2-hour hosted baseline benchmark w/ 10k requests (Ethan to schedule)
Redwood to propose canary config for dedicated pool if economics favor it
Follow-up meeting: 2025-10-28 to review benchmark results and pick scenario
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-21 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Raj (CTO Cerulean), Mira (ML Eng), Samir (Infra), Olivia (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): kickoff for poc to validate unit economics. Discussed tokens, batching, cache hit rates, dedicated vs hosted, timeline. Agreed on data requests and benchmark plan.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — size the workload, agree success criteria, and outline a benchmark + cost model. can we do a quick round of intros?
[00:18] Raj (Cerulean): sure, raj here, cto. we're trying to ship an in-app shopping assistant, expect mid-high concurrency during peak. our cost team is nervous about token burn.
[00:28] Mira (Cerulean ML): mira, i own model infra and prompt design. current proto hits about 600 tokens avg (prompt+reply) but varies a lot.
[00:38] Samir (Infra): samir, infra lead, we'll run the benchmark in our staging VPC for network parity. curious about VPC options on your private offering.
[00:50] Maya: great — ethan, do you want to add on the POC structure?
[00:55] Ethan (Redwood SE): yeah, quick one — typical POC is 4-6 weeks. we'll do three parallel streams: baseline hosted runs, then a dedicated trial if the unit econ favors it, and a hybrid config. key knobs: batching window, max batch size, kv/prefix cache and cache TTLs. i want to be explicit about metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens-per-second, cost per 1M tokens, and cache hit rate sensitivity.
[01:22] Raj: can you ballpark per-token numbers? finance wants a top-line estimate now.
[01:26] Maya: ballpark — hosted for current open Llama-style model we validated is in the range of $0.0005 - $0.0009 per token depending on sequence length and streaming inefficiencies. dedicated can drop to $0.00015 - $0.00035 per token once you amortize reserved capacity and optimize batching. those are rough, we will model three scenarios.
[01:48] Mira: that seems like a big gap — is that mainly amortization of reserved GPUs?
[01:52] Ethan: mostly yes — reserved GPU hours and better packing. also kernel selection and quantization profiles are easier to control on dedicated. plus batching: if your workload can tolerate 80-150ms extra latency you can do bigger batches and cut per-token cost substantially.
[02:12] Olivia (Product): our user SLO is 200ms for simple queries, and 400ms for longer conversational turns. is that achievable with batching?
[02:20] Ethan: depends. for short responses, aggressive batching hurts p50. but we can do hybrid: small batches for interactive paths, deferable work in background with larger batchers.
[02:33] Raj: what's the impact of KV cache hit rates? our product reuses context a lot for cart state.
[02:40] Ethan: good point — a high prefix/KV cache hit rate (70-90%) reduces repeated computation and effectively cuts tokens served back to the model. we'll model hit-rate scenarios at 20%, 50%, 80% — each has wide downstream cost impact. for example on our test maps, moving from 20% to 80% hit rate cut effective tokens by ~40%.
[03:02] Mira: what about cold starts and autoscale costs? our traffic spikes 6x in peak windows.
[03:08] Maya: we'll capture burst capacity in the cost model. Dedicated has burst policies and pre-warmed pools which cost extra but reduce cold-start latency. hosted supports burst but it's priced into usage. we'll show a runway calc: baseline + peak buffer.
[03:24] Raj: okay, success criteria — what do we need to prove in the POC?
[03:28] Ethan: propose three success criteria: 1) unit econ — achieve target <$0.0004 per token in a mid-case scenario; 2) latency — maintain p95 under 400ms for interactive flows; 3) quality — model responses match golden set within tolerance (we'll use exact-match / embedding similarity thresholds).
[03:46] Mira: embedding similarity thresholds? can you clarify metrics there?
[03:50] Ethan: we'll test a set of 200 canonical prompts and their golden replies. compute embedding similarity at 0.82+ threshold and human spot-check for hallucination rate under 1%.
[04:05] Samir: regarding network, we need SSO + audit logs. is Redwood's private control plane in our VPC or do you require a VPN?
[04:13] Maya: options: hosted (control plane managed), private (control plane in your VPC), or on-prem package. for SOC2/KMS we have integrations — we will attach compliance docs.
[04:25] Raj: good. for the benchmark runs, we want to run from our staging to get real egress metrics. ok?
[04:31] Ethan: that works. we'll provide a runner that you can deploy in your staging VPC to generate traffic and post aggregated metrics to a shared bucket.
[04:40] Olivia: timeline — what are the milestones?
[04:43] Maya: quick timeline: data & prompts shared by 10/22, baseline hosted run 10/23-10/24, review 10/28, dedicated pilot decision by 10/30, then 2-week dedicated pilot if greenlit, wrap-up and recommendations by ~11/14.
[05:00] Raj: that's tight but doable. finance needs the three-scenario spreadsheet ASAP.
[05:05] Maya: i'll send that today — scenario A (hosted conservative), B (dedicated optimized), C (hybrid with cache). we'll include sensitivity sliders for cache hit rate, batch size, and token lengths.
[05:17] Mira: when you say batch size, are you modeling both request-level batching and micro-batching inside runtime?
[05:22] Ethan: yes. we have two knobs — request batching (collecting requests for a model forward pass) and continuous micro-batching inside the runtime. both affect latency/cost differently. we'll show marginal cost curves.
[05:36] Raj: can you give me an example marginal saving?
[05:38] Ethan: on one workload we saw ~30% token-cost reduction moving batch window from 20ms to 100ms at p50 latency increase of 60ms. numbers vary by sequence length distribution.
[05:50] Olivia: what about model variants? smaller quantized models for simple intents vs full model for complex queries?
[05:56] Maya: that's part of routing policy — route trivial intents to cheaper quantized model. we'll include a routing plan with fallback and A/B measurement to track quality delta.
[06:07] Samir: encryption at rest — KMS integrations?
[06:10] Ethan: yes, KMS, HSM options for private deployments, including customer-managed keys for token logs and cache storage.
[06:18] Raj: benchmark specifics — what load shapes do you recommend?
[06:21] Ethan: recommended: 1) steady 200 qps for 30 minutes, 2) spike test 6x for 10 minutes, 3) concurrency sweep (50, 200, 1000) to measure p95 and error behavior. we'll capture per-token cost and latency distributions.
[06:36] Mira: do you simulate real prompt distributions? we have a heavy tail — few very long prompts.
[06:40] Ethan: please send histogram; we'll run both median-based and tail scenarios — tail matters for memory and kv cache.
[06:48] Raj: about instrumentation — what metrics do we see in console? token breakdown per call, cost by route, cache hits, model-level latency, errors?
[06:56] Maya: all of those. console shows token-level breakdown, per-route cost, traces and sample responses. we'll also export raw logs for your analytics.
[07:06] Olivia: are we doing any quality evals during POC?
[07:08] Ethan: yes — automatic evaluation against golden set plus 20 random human checks per run.
[07:15] Raj: any blockers?
[07:17] Mira: we need NDA for security docs — can you send SOC2 and network diagrams?
[07:21] Maya: absolutely. i'll attach SOC2 summary, network diagram, and SSO/SAML setup doc with the spreadsheet.
[07:29] Raj: ok let's recap next steps?
[07:32] Maya: 1) customer: share traffic hist and prompts by 10/22; 2) redwood: cost spreadsheet today + bench plan by 10/23; 3) run baseline hosted tests 10/23-10/24; 4) review 10/28. any other items?
[07:48] Samir: confirm runner will work from our staging VPC without opening DBs or secrets — only send metrics to s3.
[07:54] Ethan: yes, runner is stateless and emits metrics to pre-signed s3; we won't touch internal DBs.
[07:59] Olivia: good.
[08:01] Maya: perfect — thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments.

End of meeting.
